Hi Sarah — Mateo, thanks for the flag. Attaching the items below; notes inline.

Attachments:
- redwood-pii-dataflow-20280730.pdf (high-level + annotated appendix listing which subprocessors touch raw inputs)
- subprocessor-roster-20280730.csv (current snapshot; columns: name, purpose, country, data access type, SOC2 status)
- kms-ownership-summary-20280730.docx (summary of our KMS model and key custody roles)

Summary answers:  
1) Subprocessor roster: attached is the current snapshot. We do not include historical change log in outbound artifacts by default; if you require the log for audit we can provide it under an NDA — please confirm.

2) Dataflow diagram: redwood-pii-dataflow-20280730.pdf contains two pages: a public-safe diagram (page 1) and a restricted appendix (page 2) that maps PII elements to storage/processing components and names subprocessors that persist or cache unredacted inputs. For procurement intake, please review page 1; we can provide the appendix after a mutual NDA or as part of a DPA exhibit.

3) KMS custody: kms-ownership-summary explains our model: customer data-at-rest is encrypted with per-tenant keys; for hosted customers we offer both Redwood-managed keys (default) and BYOK via KMS integrations. Key material is never exported from the KMS; operational access to key rotation is limited to the crypto ops team under dual-control. We can provide an attestation letter for BYOK customers.

4) Cross-border / transfer language: we include a standard transfer annex that references SCCs or equivalent safeguards for EU transfers; for bespoke requirements we can add an exhibit. Sample wording: "Subprocessors located outside the Customer's jurisdiction will process data only under the terms of the DPA and applicable transfer safeguards." Let us know if you need the full annex text for redline.

Next steps: if those artifacts look good, Mateo can coordinate a short intake call and provide the restricted appendix under an appropriate NDA or as an exhibit to the DPA.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi all — adding a couple of security clarifications and a proposed minimal exhibit to unblock procurement.

Security clarifications:  
- Access controls: production systems are role-based. Engineers do not have access to customer PII unless explicitly authorized for an operational incident; access is logged and time-limited.
- KV / prefix caching: our inference runtime performs ephemeral KV caching for active sessions; persistent caches that could contain raw inputs are limited to a small set of logging/ingestion services described in the restricted appendix. Those services run in dedicated projects with restricted network egress.
- Audit evidence: we can provide scoped audit logs for onboarding review (export csv) showing which Redwood identities accessed relevant storage components during a two-week window.

Proposed next steps to finish procurement quickly:  
1) I’ll upload the restricted appendix to a shared Drive folder and provide a short attestation for KMS controls. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_dataflow_diagram
2) If MerchantGateway is comfortable, sign the attached DPA exhibit (DocuSign template) which binds the restricted appendix as an exhibit. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/templates/ABCDEFG-merchant-dpa
3) If they need the historical subprocessor change log or additional audit windows, we can scope that as an addendum and provide under a mutual NDA.

If those steps work I can prepare the attestation and pin the exact audit window we’ll export. Mateo — can you coordinate with Procurement on signing the exhibit?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
